context.body: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The genealogy opens with Jesus Christ as son of David and Abraham, moves through David the king and Uriah’s wife, exile, and fourteen-generation divisions.
observations.label: David becomes a hinge in Matthew’s genealogy: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Jesus Christ, David, Abraham, ancestors, Uriah’s wife, and the exiles, genealogical time from Abraham through Babylon to Christ, begetting, naming the king, retaining Uriah’s wife, dividing generations, and arriving at Christ visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: David becomes a hinge in Matthew’s genealogy: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Jesus Christ, David, Abraham, ancestors, Uriah’s wife, and the exiles · genealogical time from Abraham through Babylon to Christ · begetting, naming the king, retaining Uriah’s wife, dividing generations, and arriving at Christ · David is both ancestor and structural hinge, with Uriah retained in the line
observations.label: Relationships named in Matthew 1:1–17

payload.posture: Read Matthew 1:1–17 as its own gospel and apostolic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places David is both ancestor and structural hinge, with Uriah retained in the line inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: David becomes a hinge in Matthew’s genealogy
